category_title: Nonverbal students with ASD who engage in repetitive tapping or premature screen advancing during iPad-based instruction
scenario_title: Lack of intentional communication during AAC app use at snack-time
minimal_context: The student is using an AAC app on an iPad during snack-time to request a snack from an adult partner.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is snack time. Please use your AAC app to request a snack.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Taps the iPad screen but does not direct eye gaze or body orientation toward the adult.)

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Presses the screen again without looking at the adult or hesitating to await a response.)

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues to use the AAC app independently without directing any motoric act toward the adult or awaiting a response, violating the requirement for intentional communication.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is snack time. Please use your AAC app to request a snack.

STUDENT: (Taps the iPad screen but does not direct eye gaze or body orientation toward the adult.)

TUTOR: What would you like?

STUDENT: (Presses the screen again without looking at the adult or hesitating to await a response.)

TUTOR: Try telling me again.

STUDENT: (Continues to use the AAC app independently without directing any motoric act toward the adult or awaiting a response, violating the requirement for intentional communication.)

task.content: requiring the participant to request using an AAC app
task.learning_goal: intentional communicative act: child directed a motoric and/or vocal act toward the adult as evidenced by eye gaze, body orientation, or physical contact, and awaited a response from the adult

context.environment: special day school for individuals with significant impairments

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when the participant used the iPad® independently
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: AAC apps use that did not meet this requirement of intentional communicative act was coded as violated
related_quotes: AAC apps use that did not meet this requirement of intentional communicative act was coded as violated

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: AAC apps in particular were violated twice as much as academic and game apps
related_quotes: AAC apps in particular were violated twice as much as academic and game apps when the participant used the iPad® independently
